label: copy-phase input n (fed-back n during recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is n, meaning the model is reading back its own previously emitted n. It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token. The plain rule (copy phase and input n) gets 100% recall at 0.74 precision. Adding recall_idx >= 2 (leaving out the first fed-back token, which is orig(0)=n) raises precision to 0.84. Those first-position n inputs fire only weakly and hold 3% of the mass. Magnitude is largest when the n was an early original token (for example orig(2), read back at recall_idx 3) and many outputs are still left. Activations shrink toward the end of the sequence and on later repeats of n. About 16% of copy-phase n inputs stay inactive, mostly when n is near the end of the sequence.

issues: The core claims hold. Dev profile: 0 activations in the original phase and at the delimiter. In the copy phase in_tok == n accounts for 100% of activations and mass. Copy phase plus input n scores test P 0.737, R 1.000. With recall_idx >= 2 added, test P 0.843, R 0.934, F1 0.886, mass recall 0.967, matching the reported scores.
The claim about the first position is right. recall_idx == 1 with input n has P 0.26 and holds 3.1% of the mass.

Minor overstatement: 'inactive steps are mostly an n near the end' is only partly true. False positives are spread out. Precision is 0.78 at to_go == 0, 0.83 at to_go 1-3 and 0.93 at to_go >= 4. Short sequences also fire less: L == 3 has P 0.41 and L == 4 has P 0.75, against about 0.86-0.89 for L >= 5. Both trends are gradual, not a distinct class.

No systematic false-positive or miss class found. Precision stays near 0.81-0.93 across prev_tok digit or vowel, out_tok digit or n, n_digits, repeated n (in_count >= 2), prev_tok == n and first_tok == n. Restricting to L >= 5 (F1 0.867) or to_go >= 1 (F1 0.797) lowers F1, so the original predicate is close to the best one available.
